reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Billing dispute tickets doubled from ~600 to over 1,200/month starting August 2026 (F-05), not because dispute handling is slow (within SLA, F-01) or a tariff changed (none occurred, F-04), but because the billing import + validation step is issuing incorrect bills: the majority of disputed bills (1,785 of 3,025, ~59%) are built from ACTUAL meter reads rather than estimated ones (F-03), showing the defect occurs when accepted reads are processed into bills, not only when reads are missing. A field manual-read completion shortfall (0.88 vs 0.95 target, 9,200 accounts, F-02) is a secondary contributor driving estimate-substitution disputes for the remaining accounts.
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month to 1,180-1,260/month starting August 2026 (E-05), not from slow handling (within SLA, E-01) or a tariff change (none occurred, E-04). For 1,184 of 1,240 disputed ESTIMATED-read accounts, AMI reads were received and exported but rejected at billing import under rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-13), which compares raw register values to 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling='none'; because v4.2-firmware meters (rollout 2026-06) record in 0.1 m3 units rather than m3 (E-14), their reads appear roughly 10x too high and are spuriously flagged high-consumption, forcing estimate substitution (E-12). This confirmed mechanism does not yet explain the majority of disputes (1,785 of 3,025, ACTUAL-read bills, E-03).
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
